metadata.title: Profiles of facilitators’ beliefs about collaboration and how they relate to experience, job satisfaction, self-efficacy, and willingness to innovate

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study collected survey data from 373 invited mathematics teacher PD facilitators in Germany and analyzed a final analytic sample of 190 experienced facilitators. The manuscript explicitly states that probability sampling was not used, so the results are not intended to be population-representative; however, it does not report any complex survey weighting variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife). Because the analysis is based on person-centred latent profile analysis (LPA) and group comparisons (MANOVA/ANOVA), the paper does not describe applying sampling weights to estimate population parameters. Therefore, no explicit weighting strategy is documented, and the findings should be interpreted as descriptive/associational within the recruited facilitator cohort rather than as weighted estimates for all German facilitators.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This study does not use ILSA cognitive achievement outcomes with Plausible Values; instead, it models facilitator belief scales and related Likert/composite constructs (e.g., collaboration beliefs, job satisfaction, self-efficacy, willingness to innovate). Because the dependent variables are non-PV survey measures, PV handling is not applicable by design. Missing data handling is addressed through exclusion of participants with missing data, so PV-related reporting gaps are not relevant here.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Data were collected in August 2023 prior to the start of the QuaMath facilitator preparation programme. Of 373 invited facilitators, 23 did not respond and 18 were excluded due to missing data, yielding 332 respondents. The analysis then restricted to facilitators with prior experience (at least one-year experience as a facilitator), resulting in a final analytic sample of 190 experienced facilitators. The sample includes facilitators from 15 of the 16 German federal states; no probability sampling was used.

main_findings.dataset_used: QuaMath facilitator survey (Germany, Aug 2023; mathematics teacher PD facilitators)
main_findings.target_variable: Latent profiles of collaboration beliefs (3-class LPA)
main_findings.performance_metrics: LPA fit: AIC = 759.80; BIC = 805.26; entropy = 0.82; minimum class membership probability = 0.84; maximum = 0.95; bootstrap likelihood ratio test p < .01; class sizes: 26 (13.7%), 38 (20.0%), 126 (66.3%). Additional analysis (Differences in self-efficacy and willingness to innovate across collaboration profiles): MANOVA: F(16, 356) = 39.506, p < .001, partial η2 = 0.64, Wilk’s Λ = 0.13. Follow-up ANOVAs: self-efficacy F(2, 187) = 7.637, p < .001, partial η2 = 0.08; willingness to innovate F(2, 187) = 125.8, p < .001, partial η2 = 0.07. Post-hoc: Moderate vs Enthusiasts self-efficacy MDiff = −0.31 (95% CI [−0.49, −0.12]), Cohen’s d = −0.75; willingness to innovate MDiff = −0.23 (95% CI [−0.34, −0.08]), p < .05, Cohen’s d = −0.67. No profile differences for teaching experience, facilitator experience, or job satisfaction. Limitation: willingness-to-innovate scale reliability is low (ω = 0.52).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using QuaMath facilitator survey data from Germany, the study leveraged collaboration beliefs with teachers, with facilitators, and among teachers during PD to identify latent profiles, finding a three-class solution (Selective Collaborators, Moderate Collaborators, Collaboration Enthusiasts) with clear classification quality (entropy = 0.82). This indicates that facilitator collaboration beliefs are meaningfully heterogeneous and can be targeted in PD preparation rather than treated as a single uniform trait.

data.outcome_summary: This study used a QuaMath facilitator survey in Germany (Aug 2023) with 190 experienced mathematics teacher PD facilitators to identify person-centred profiles of collaboration beliefs and to examine how these profiles relate to facilitator characteristics. The best-fitting three-class latent profile analysis (AIC = 759.80; BIC = 805.26; entropy = 0.82) distinguished Selective Collaborators, Moderate Collaborators, and Collaboration Enthusiasts based on collaboration beliefs with teachers, with facilitators, and among teachers during PD. Group differences were tested with MANOVA, which was significant for the combined dependent variables (F(16,356)=39.506, p<.001, partial η2=0.64). Follow-up tests showed significant profile differences for self-efficacy and willingness to innovate, but not for teaching experience, facilitator experience, or job satisfaction. The analysis is not an ILSA/PV-based achievement ML study, uses no survey weights, and willingness-to-innovate has low reliability (ω=0.52), limiting precision and causal interpretation.
